title: Cover and Secure Roof Openings During Demolition
summary: A demolition foreman died after a 35-foot fall through a roof opening that was covered only by loose plywood. When he moved the sheet, the hole was open. Cover roof openings, secure the cover, and guard the area.
talking_points: A crew had cut a 44 by 78 inch hole in a flat roof so a crane could lower a cable through it. When the task ended, a 48 by 96 inch plywood sheet was laid over it. It was not nailed or screwed down and had no railing around it.
The foreman walked onto the roof to get that plywood for another job. He wore no harness. When he moved the sheet, he fell 35 feet to the concrete floor.
Cover temporary roof openings and secure the cover so it cannot be moved by accident.
Add guardrails around the opening or cover so no one can remove or displace the cover. Rails also give you a tie-off option.
Never take material that is covering a hole unless the hole is made safe first.
Get training in fall hazards and fall protection, even if you have worked for the company for years.
A competent person should do scheduled and unscheduled inspections. A competent person can find hazards and has the authority to fix them quickly.
site_hazards_to_check: Plywood or other covers lying over holes without fasteners or markings
Roof openings with no railing around them
Materials stored or staged on top of covered openings
Workers on the roof without a harness or tie-off point
No one assigned to inspect the work area for hazards
discussion_questions: What openings did we make in the roof or floors, and how is each one covered and secured?
Who is the competent person who inspects the site today?
What do you do if you need material that is covering an opening?
